question.text: If the relation between the direction ratios of two lines in $\mathbb{R}^3$ are given by $l+m+n=0,2 / m+2 m n-l n=0$ then the angle between the lines is ( $I, m$, $n$ have their usual meaning)

solution.text:
Hint : Quadratic in $\frac{m}{n}: 2\left(\frac{m}{n}\right)^2-\frac{m}{n}-1=0 \Rightarrow \frac{m}{n}=1,-\frac{1}{2}$ $\Rightarrow \mathrm{n}=\mathrm{m}$ or $\mathrm{n}=-2 \mathrm{~m} \& I=-\mathrm{m}-\mathrm{n}, \Rightarrow I: \mathrm{m}: \mathrm{n} \Rightarrow-2: 1: 1$ or $1: 1-2$
$\therefore$ Angle $=\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{-2}{\sqrt{6}} \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\left(\frac{-1}{\sqrt{6}}\right)\right)=\cos \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)=\frac{2 \pi}{3}$
